governance.decisionForum: King’s Edge Portfolio Board, with the team’s organisational, workforce and professional-practice arrangements governed through the relevant Digital and IT forums.
governance.decisionScope: Material decisions about the team’s remit, the four funded Year One posts, the shared capabilities that sit outside those posts, role grading and recruitment route, whether solution architecture is covered within the Senior Backend & Integration Engineer post or separately, staffing and capacity, leadership and decision rights, demand intake and prioritisation, the evidence the first year must generate about team shape and institutional capability, any material increase in the first-year Hub scope that would compete with the King’s Edge roadmap, product and delivery practices, interfaces with specialist Digital and IT functions, evidence-based decisions to expand the team, handover criteria and enduring institutional ownership.
governance.businessAsUsualOwner: TBC – Digital and IT product development capability owner
governance.businessAsUsualOwnershipNote: The capability is expected to sit within Digital and IT. The Year One funded core is four explicit posts: Senior Backend & Integration Engineer, Middleweight Full-Stack Engineer, UX/UI Designer and QA Engineer. Product ownership, delivery coordination, DevOps/platform support, service design, business analysis, user research, solution architecture where not covered by the senior engineer, and other specialist assurance functions sit outside that four-post core and must be provided through named shared or existing capacity unless evidence demonstrates a further funded gap. The enduring organisational home, recurrent staffing, professional leadership and relationship to the Digital Student Experience Hub product and platform ownership under 4.1.2 should be confirmed as the operating model is proven. King’s Edge remains the principal substantive product demand and the September 2027 Hub is a focused first live release. Any material expansion in integration depth or team size should follow evidence from delivery and live use.
